assignment.title: Retrying failed jobs
assignment.instructions: Design how the practice background worker retries a job that fails. Hand in a short design note.

sections.heading: Instructions
paragraphs: Submit as a text message plus one file, by Friday.

sections.heading: Criteria
paragraphs: Idempotency keys, including how they are stored

submission.text: Hi, here are my notes on retrying failed jobs for the practice worker. The full write-up is in retries.docx, which has the policy and how jobs are tagged.

sections.heading: Retry policy
paragraphs: A job that raises an error is put back on the queue and tried again after a delay. The delay grows with each attempt: 2 seconds, then 4, 8, 16 and 32, which is exponential backoff with a base of 2 seconds. To stop many failed jobs from retrying at the same moment, each delay has up to 20 percent of random jitter added. Jobs are attempted at most five times.
The backoff matters because most failures in this worker are temporary, such as a slow upstream service. Waiting longer each time gives the other side room to recover instead of hammering it.

sections.heading: Idempotency keys
paragraphs: A retried job might run twice if the first attempt succeeded but its acknowledgement was lost. To make that harmless, every job carries an idempotency key, and the handler for each job type is written so that running it again with the same key has no additional effect.
